title: Cycle detection across the rule graph
preamble:
# Cycle detection across the rule graph

DS's cross-cutting stance
against unbounded computation, and the
compile-time cycle-detection pass that closes the
one enforcement gap at the rule-graph level.
Zero grammar surface — this is purely a compiler
analysis over already-parsed rules.

Paired with:

- [LSCO] — the bounded scope this doc
  systematises.
- [LLOG] — the
  worst-case cycle shape lives here (rules that
  defeat each other through negation).
- [LCRS] —
  `cooldown` partially mitigates call cycles but
  doesn't prevent them.
- [LERR.1] — cycle rejection is
  a compile error and fits the compile-error
  policy exactly.
